title: A group of prime order is cyclic
statement: Let $p$ be a prime natural number and let $G$ be a group (a set with an associative multiplication, an identity, and inverses) whose underlying set is finite [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set], with exactly $p$ elements. Then $G$ is cyclic: there is $g\in G$ such that every element of $G$ is an integer power of $g$.
